You move each individual finger, starting with the pinky with A,S,D,F, and and the Space Bar(thumb). You can also grab by pressing Mouse 1. This closes all the fingers and the thumb at the same time. Thank you comments section for reminding me about Mouse 1.

To move an entire arm up or down you spin the scroll wheel on your mouse.

To  move an entire arm forward or back you just move the mouse forward or back.

To rotate the wrist you hold down one of the mouse buttons then start moving the mouse left or right. The wrist only rotates on a simple R axis. [i]It does not move like a regular wrist that can also twist forward or backwards. It only rotates left or right.[/i]  To move the whole arm left or right you move the mouse left or right without holding a mouse button.

In order to switch hands you press shift. You can only move one hand at a time and the other hand stays where you left it, even if you are holding something (nice feature). If you bump into something with one hand while the other hand is holding it (think loading a magaazine into a gun) then it will move slightly. This is incredibly frustrating as you try again and again while your other hand moves ever so slightly with each try.

There is a button to switch your control from each individual hand to your head or your feet. The head works just fine but switching to feet does absolutely nothing at the time of this review.*

It all began innocently enough.

A few friends and I were browsing Steam one evening, looking for something stupid to play—a cheap laugh, a quick distraction, something chaotic and low-stakes. Hand Simulator came up, accompanied by a slew of cursed gameplay videos and comments like “worst controls ever” and “why do my fingers do this?” Naturally, we were intrigued. We downloaded it, booted it up, and within minutes, my descent into madness had begun.

At first, it was hilarious. The game, if you can call it that, puts you in control of a single disembodied hand with a set of controls that seem specifically designed to mimic the feeling of having never used a hand before in your life. Moving individual fingers, rotating the wrist, trying to pick up a gun, milk a cow, or pour tea—tasks that seemed trivial in real life turned into Herculean trials of coordination and patience.

But what began as laughter soon twisted into obsession. I couldn’t not get that revolver loaded. I had to beat my friend in Russian roulette. I spent nights—entire nights—practicing the arcane art of wrist rotation and index finger flexion, rewiring my brain to master the impossible. My keyboard became a battlefield. WASD were no longer movement keys—they were fingers. Q and E were now wrist control. I dreamt in keystrokes. I woke up with cramped hands and deep, existential dread.

My relationships suffered. My friends, who had introduced me to the game, left long ago—scarred, but wiser. I remained. I missed my sister’s wedding to attend a virtual hand-to-hand combat tournament. My cat no longer recognizes me. My keyboard is now missing half its keys, worn smooth from frantic finger spasms.

And the worst part? There’s no reward. There’s no boss fight, no leaderboard, no real sense of accomplishment. Just the empty, hollow satisfaction of successfully pouring a cup of tea—only to immediately knock it over and start again.

They say games are supposed to be fun, a source of joy, an escape. Hand Simulator is none of these. It’s a mirror held up to our own limitations, a stark reminder that coordination is an illusion and hands are a lie. It didn’t just ruin my life—it made me question the very essence of being.

So to those who are curious, to those who think, “How bad can it really be?”—run. Run far. Because once you enter the world of Hand Simulator, you’ll never look at your fingers the same way again.

Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)

"Hand Simulator" on Steam is a one-of-a-kind physics-based multiplayer game that pushes the boundaries of dexterity, coordination, and patience. Developed by HFM Games, this title takes players on a comical and challenging journey through various hand-related tasks, resulting in both moments of triumph and laughter.

Gameplay:
As the name suggests, "Hand Simulator" centers around controlling virtual hands with precision and skill. The game offers a variety of scenarios and challenges, ranging from simple tasks like picking up objects and operating tools to complex tasks such as shooting firearms, flying helicopters, and driving vehicles. The controls mimic real hand movements, adding an element of realism and hilarity to the overall experience.

Multiplayer Shenanigans:
The multiplayer aspect of "Hand Simulator" is where the true magic happens. Interacting with other players, each attempting to complete tasks with their own clumsy hand movements, leads to a riotous and chaotic experience. Whether you're cooperating to achieve objectives or engaging in friendly competitions, the unpredictable nature of multiplayer interactions never fails to generate moments of laughter and shared amusement.

Sandbox Mode and Workshop Support:
In addition to the pre-designed scenarios, "Hand Simulator" offers a sandbox mode that allows players to create custom levels and challenges. This feature, combined with workshop support, provides an endless stream of player-created content, adding to the game's replayability and longevity.

Accessibility and Learning Curve:
While the concept of controlling virtual hands may seem straightforward, the learning curve in "Hand Simulator" can be steep, especially for newcomers. Mastering the hand movements and getting used to the physics-based controls can take time, but it also contributes to the game's charm and sense of accomplishment as players improve their skills over time.

Graphics and Sound:
The game's graphics are simple but effective, providing a clean and uncluttered environment for players to focus on the task at hand (pun intended). The sound design complements the gameplay well, with playful and whimsical audio cues that add to the overall fun factor.

Community and Engagement:
The "Hand Simulator" community is vibrant and active, with players frequently sharing their hilarious and epic moments through videos and streams. The game's humorous nature fosters a positive and inclusive environment where players can bond over their hand-controlled escapades.

Conclusion:
"Hand Simulator" is a refreshingly original and enjoyable multiplayer game that delivers laughter and amusement in abundance. With its challenging controls, unpredictable physics, and multiplayer madness, it offers a unique and hilarious experience for players willing to embrace the wackiness. The ability to create and share custom content further enhances the game's appeal, making it an entertaining choice for friends looking to embark on a quirky adventure together.
